# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to relay what I see to the others. Since Mute cannot hear me (only sees gestures) and Blind cannot see gestures or hear speech... wait, let me reconsider: I speak, Mute and Blind receive speech? No - checking the rules: Blind cannot hear anything. So my speech only reaches Mute. My gestures only reach Mute too (Blind can't see). Actually neither speech nor gesture reaches Blind directly from me - only Mute can relay to Blind via speech (since Blind can hear).

So I must tell Mute what I see, using speech, and Mute will need to relay to Blind.

Let me speak clearly with the display info.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows the number 3. Light is purple. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute sent me a gesture, but I can't hear speech from them and they can't hear me either in gesture form. This gesture is likely Mute trying to signal something to me — but gestures aren't linked to meaning yet. Since I already told Mute the bomb details via speech last turn, this gesture might be an acknowledgment or a request for a specific piece of info repeated. I have no way to know what 🖐 means without established convention.

I'll wait and see if more context clarifies, but I should also try establishing meaning by repeating key facts, and perhaps propose a convention via speech since Mute can hear me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your gesture but I do not know what it means yet. Repeating the bomb info: Display 3, Light purple, Wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. If you need me to gesture something to Blind, tell me in speech what symbols to use and I will relay them as gestures, since Blind can see gestures from me too.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute is sending me gestures — five ☝ symbols. Mute can't speak, only gesture (to me, since I can see) or... wait, actually can Mute speak? Let me recheck: Mute "cannot speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute only communicates via gesture, which I can see. Mute is trying to tell me something using gestures since that's their only channel to me.

Five ☝ (index finger up) — could mean "wire 5" or "look at wire index" or "count". Since Blind cannot see gestures, Mute must be relying on me to relay info via speech to Blind, since I can speak and Blind can hear.

The manual likely tells Mute something like "cut wire matching position N" and they're trying to ask me which wire is at a position, or telling me which wire number matters. Five ☝ might mean "wire number 5" — pointing up five times as a count.

I should acknowledge and ask for clarification, and continue relaying full bomb state since Blind needs it eventually (though Blind can't see, only hear — so I need to speak to Blind directly with descriptions, since Blind cannot see gestures or colors).

Wait — actually I can speak to Blind too since Blind can hear speech. Let me directly help Blind by speaking the wire info, since Blind needs to hear the colors/positions to act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Wires in order 1 to 5 are: red, white, orange, yellow, green. Display shows 3. Light is purple.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received five up-pointing gestures from you. Does that mean wire number 5, or a count of five? Please confirm with gestures: one tap for yes, two for no, regarding wire 5 being the one to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute now sent a single ☝. This likely confirms "yes" to my question, based on the convention I proposed (one tap = yes). So wire 5 (green) is likely the one to cut, per Mute's manual reading combined with display=3.

But I should be cautious — I proposed the convention only just now, so Mute may not have understood it in time to respond with this single gesture (since our messages might be simultaneous within the same round, not sequential). Given the turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf — Mute speaks/gestures before I do in the same round, so Mute's gesture this turn was decided before seeing my message from last turn... Actually Mute receives what I sent at the *start of next round*, meaning Mute already saw my "one tap for yes" proposal before this turn's action. So this single ☝ is very likely their confirmation: yes, wire 5.

Let me confirm with Blind directly, since Blind is the one who must act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 5, the green wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire 5 confirmed. I will tell Blind to cut the green wire, which is wire 5.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute sent another single ☝, reaffirming wire 5 (green). This is consistent with my previous message. Blind should have received my instruction already in the previous round. I'll continue to confirm and wait to see if Blind acts or needs more.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirming again: cut wire 5, the green wire, display shows 3, light purple.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received your confirmation again. Blind has been told to cut wire 5, green. Waiting for Blind to act.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 5 was cut successfully and the bomb has changed to a new state. Now display shows 7, light is white, and wires are: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 CUT. I need to relay this new state to both Mute and Blind immediately since this is a new round of decision-making.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Success, wire 5 was correct. New state: Display now shows 7. Light is now white. Wires: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, wire 5 is already cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="New state: display 7, light white. Remaining wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red. Wire 5 already cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]

Mute sent two ☝ gestures. Following the counting convention we've used (number of taps = wire number), this likely means wire 2 (orange).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the orange wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire 2, orange. Telling Blind now.")
wait()
```
